summary: Per-tenant webhook delivery acknowledgements with chained HMAC proofs and rotation policy for SIEM ingestion
description:
Issue summary: Customer requests a verifiable delivery acknowledgement mechanism for per-tenant webhook SIEM ingests. They want an ordered delivery receipt stream where each batch includes an HMAC chain proof (previous batch HMAC included) and metadata proving which tenant key was used. The proof must survive key rotation and include a rotation log so auditors can validate continuity.

Impact: Finova uses our live audit webhook to feed their SIEM for fraud analytics. They need cryptographic delivery receipts that 3rd-party auditors can verify during quarterly audits. Without this proof they cannot meet bank audit requirements and may delay go-live.

Environment: prod-us-east, tenant: finova-bank-prod

Steps to reproduce / current behavior:
1) Customer subscribes to /v1/audit/webhook endpoint with per-tenant HMAC header configuration.
2) They observe deliveries succeed (2xx) but receipts do not contain a chained HMAC or explicit key rotation metadata.
3) Customer requests a backfill and an on-demand manifest for the last 72 hours that demonstrates chaining across rotate_key events.

Attachments / logs provided by customer: base64 sample webhook payload (redacted), timestamped delivery log lines, and a short extract of their auditor checklist.

Requested deliverables:
- Specification of the HMAC-chain format we will include in the delivery receipt header (examples and canonical serialization)
- A per-tenant rotation log export (tz-normalized) for the last 90 days with key IDs, rotate timestamps, and signer fingerprints
- An on-demand 72-hour backfill manifest with resume tokens and chain proofs that auditors can validate offline
- Instructions for the customer on verification steps and an example verification script

Customer timeline: Q2 external audit window, requests evidence by 2026-03-18.
comments: 2026-03-10 Diego Marquez: Acknowledged. Assigning to eng-sre to validate current webhook proxy capabilities and whether rotation metadata is being propagated to delivery receipts. SLA noted — customer needs evidence by 2026-03-18.

2026-03-10 Support Engineer (Priya Singh): First pass: our current webhook delivery receipt only returns a delivery_id and status. There is an internal field hmac_signature but it is ephemeral and not chained. I'm opening an internal investigation to confirm where rotate_key events are logged and whether we can synthesize a chain proof for historical batches.

2026-03-11 SRE (Liam O'Connor): Investigation notes: rotate_key events are emitted to audit-ledger v2 with event_type 'kms.rotate' and include tenant_id and key_id. Delivery proxy logs include a header X-Delivery-HMAC and X-Delivery-KeyId but we do not currently include previous_batch_hmac. Storage: recent deliveries are persisted in s3://audit-archive/tenant=finova-bank/partition=2026-03-10/ . Can generate backfill from there if customer approves export format.

2026-03-11 Diego Marquez: Action items: (1) produce an HMAC-chain serialization spec and send a sample for customer verification; (2) prepare a signed rotation log extract for Finova for last 90 days; (3) scope on-demand backfill with redaction for PII. Est. ETA for artifacts: 2026-03-13.

2026-03-12 Customer (Finova Bank - Compliance): Clarification: rotation log must show both old and new key fingerprints and the authority that initiated rotation. Backfill must preserve event ordering and include resume tokens for partial replay. We require SHA256-HMAC with tenant-scoped KEK as the signer (we will provide key_id mapping).

2026-03-12 Priya Singh: Note: We need Finova to provide the tenant key mapping file (tenant -> external key reference) so we can annotate the rotation log with their canonical key identifiers. Also need confirmation if they prefer JSONL or Parquet for the backfill manifest.
2026-03-12 Customer: JSONL is preferred for quick validation by their auditors. They will upload the key mapping to the secure portal by EOD 2026-03-12.

2026-03-13 SRE (Liam O'Connor): Prototype HMAC-chain serialization: base64(HMAC(curr_batch || prev_hmac || batch_ts)) with header fields: X-Chain-HMAC, X-Prev-HMAC, X-Batch-Ts, X-Key-Id. Generated sample attached to ticket (internal). Confirming that the chain can be retroactively generated from archive if we include archived deliveries in order. Discussed performance and cost of backfill generation — estimated 2-3 hours of job time for 72h window.

2026-03-13 Diego Marquez: Next steps for delivery: (A) send specimen HMAC-chain spec and verification script to Finova; (B) schedule backfill export job pending customer approval of JSONL format and SFTP or presigned S3 transfer; (C) produce rotation log extract signed with platform signing key and include KMS attestation reference; (D) document verification steps for auditors. Assigned owner: Priya for artifacts, Liam for backfill job. ETA: 2026-03-15 for artifacts, 2026-03-16 for backfill run.

2026-03-13 Customer: Confirmed they will approve JSONL and will upload tenant key mapping by 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC. Asked whether we can include a tamper-evident manifest with SHA256 digests per file — they require this for their chain-of-custody evidence.

2026-03-13 Priya Singh: Confirming we will include a manifest.json with per-file SHA256 digests and a platform signature (ED25519). Will also attach KMS export proof (kms:AttestationRef) per rotation entry. Preparing template now.
2026-03-13 Diego Marquez: Blocking: need legal approval to include key fingerprints in export for tenant-managed keys. Looping in Security and Legal.
requested_outputs: HMAC-chain serialization spec with canonical examples and verification script
90-day per-tenant key rotation log (tz-normalized) with key_id and signer fingerprint
72-hour JSONL backfill manifest with resume tokens and per-file SHA256 digests (tamper-evident)
Verification instructions for auditors including sample verification commands

Security to provide KMS attestation snippet for rotation events

Support to deliver verification script and run a live validation session with Finova auditors
